evidence: Plan: 'For a permanent setting, the named ticket is a standing admission ticket.' The plan cites this as the convention from docs/architecture.md and sunset_markers.py.

Searching the repo for 'standing admission' finds it only in docs/adr/0123 (this change's own output). docs/architecture.md never mentions it.
docs/architecture.md:649 still shows the grammar as '<reason or ticket id>', but the code (`_SUNSET_RE`) requires a ticket id.
findings.finding: The plan presents 'a standing admission ticket for a permanent setting' as an established convention and cites docs/architecture.md §Mechanism-delta ratchet and sunset_markers.py for it. Neither source defines that pattern. sunset_markers.py's docstring says the ticket-id grammar was introduced specifically so an admission could no longer be permanent. A ticket that never closes brings back exactly that. The plan gives no positive reason why that is acceptable for this key, and it does not record the pattern in the ratchet documentation. Future permanent mechanisms will either rediscover the workaround on their own or misread it as a loophole.
findings.location: Problem § 'Convention for admitting a mechanism added after the baseline froze'; docs/architecture.md §'The marker'
scenarios: A later contributor adds another permanent config key, reads docs/architecture.md, finds no guidance for permanent admissions, and either writes a prose-only marker (which fails lint) or invents a different scheme.
A reviewer or triage sweep sees a never-closing priority-4 ticket and reads it as a way around the sunset rule instead of a sanctioned pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a plan step that updates docs/architecture.md §'The marker' in two ways. (a) Correct the grammar line to say the reason must open with a ticket id. (b) Add a short paragraph: a mechanism the operator has decided is permanent names a dedicated standing admission ticket. That ticket stays open and unclaimed while the mechanism exists and closes only in the change that removes the mechanism and runs `--update-stale`, which keeps the close-refusal as a two-way door. Cite ADR 0123 / cankered-cloistered-bittern as the first instance. Then reword the plan's Convention paragraph so it says this change establishes and documents the pattern, rather than claiming the pattern already exists.
